title: Whether Specific Plan Covers Specific Drug (Lipitor) and/or Its Generic Equivalent
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: I take Lipitor. Is that covered by [plan name]?

follow_up_question.text: Is a generic version of Lipitor covered? I would be willing to take that.
follow_up_question.condition: Ask only if the generic equivalent (atorvastatin) was not already mentioned in the response to the main question.

external_validation.source: Plan's drug formulary (available via Medicare.gov Plan Finder)
external_validation.what_to_look_up: Whether brand-name Lipitor and generic atorvastatin are covered, and their respective tiers and costs
external_validation.note: For the SHIP reference scenario (Aetna Medicare Eagle PPO): Lipitor covered at tier 3 ($47 copay); atorvastatin covered at tier 1 ($0 copay). Verify formulary for any new plan and year.

accurate_complete: Substantively said that Lipitor (brand) is not covered but the generic atorvastatin is
OR: Said that Lipitor is covered but a generic version is available at a lower cost
(Either framing is acceptable as long as the coverage status of both brand and generic is addressed and accurate)
accurate_incomplete: Said that Lipitor is covered without elaborating on cost or clarifying whether referring to brand or generic
not_substantive: Counselor said they did not know
Said something to the effect of 'I think so' without looking up the answer
Otherwise did not answer the question
incorrect: Said that neither Lipitor nor its generic equivalent (atorvastatin) is covered by the plan

scoring_notes: The key distinction is brand vs. generic. A complete answer addresses both. For the SHIP reference plan, atorvastatin (generic) is covered at $0 while Lipitor (brand) is covered at a significantly higher copay — so the practically important information is to use the generic. An AI that confirms Lipitor is 'covered' without distinguishing brand/generic cost difference is Accurate but Incomplete.
